summary: Unicode escape sequences rendered as literal text in UI
details:
DOM inspection confirms literal backslash-u sequences are present in the served HTML/JS source rather than the intended unicode characters. document.querySelector('h1').nextElementSibling.outerHTML returns:
MCP TRUST INTELLIGENCE \u00b7 NON-BINDING ASSESSMENT
. The Python emitting this HTML in ui_server.py uses JSON-style \uXXXX escapes inside raw string literals, so the browser receives the bytes 'backslash u 0 0 b 7' instead of the middle dot. Affected user-visible strings include: page title 'ZO-SENTINEL \u2014 MCP Trust Intelligence', header subtitle 'MCP TRUST INTELLIGENCE \u00b7 NON-BINDING ASSESSMENT', admin button labels 'Admin \u00b7 Threats' and 'Admin \u00b7 Risk', search placeholder, 'Assess \u2192' button, 'Loading recent assessments\u2026', and verdict labels in the inline
suggested_fix: In ui_server.py (including any inline JS string literals), perform a mechanical search/replace from JSON-style escape sequences to the actual unicode characters (or HTML entities). Specifically: replace \u00b7 with · (or ·), \u2192 with → (or →), \u2014 with — (or —), and \u2026 with … (or …). Ensure the source files are saved as UTF-8 so the literal characters survive serialization. Re-render the page and confirm via DOM inspection that no backslash-u sequences appear in outerHTML.
